newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch consumer confidence rises in September.
newsitem.headline: Dutch consumer confidence rises in September.

text.p: The Dutch consumer confidence index rose to 8 in September from 5 in August, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said.
DUTCH CONSUMER CONFIDENCE Sept 96 Aug 96 Sept 95
NOTE - The index can vary between -100 and +100 points with zero as the neutral midpoint. A negative index value indicates a majority of the consumers polled by the CBS are pessimistic.
The total index is made up of two subindices which reflect consumers' feelings about the general economic climate and about their personal finances and spending plans:
NOTES - The CBS noted that the September data showed a continuation of the gradual increase in consumer confidence which has been under way since April.
The rise in September was entirely due to a rise in the subindex measuring confidence in the economic climate.
The CBS said this coincided with the recent publication of favourable data on the economy, but added that its September survey of consumers took place before budget day (September 17).
The subindex measuring consumers' sentiment about their own finances and their willingness to purchase goods actually fell, but the CBS said this was normal in September.
